Polysomnography Report
Procedure: Attended, full-night diagnostic polysomnography.
Clinical Indication: Excessive daytime sleepiness, reported snoring, and witnessed apneas.
This was a technically adequate overnight diagnostic polysomogram. Total sleep time was 345 minutes with a sleep efficiency of 82%. Sleep architecture was abnormal due to significant sleep fragmentation. REM sleep was reduced, comprising only 10% of total sleep time.
Frequent respiratory events were noted throughout the night. The overall Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) was 42 events per hour, which is in the severe range. These events were predominantly obstructive apneas and hypopneas, and they were more severe during REM sleep. This was associated with significant oxygen desaturation, with a nadir SpO2 of 78%. The patients baseline oxygen saturation was 95%. No significant periodic limb movements were noted.
Impression: The findings are consistent with severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).
A follow-up appointment is recommended to discuss treatment options, including positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy. A subsequent PAP titration study under polysomnography is indicated to determine the optimal pressure for treatment.

Clinical History: 29-year-old female with a known history of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), presenting with new-onset proteinuria and hematuria. Biopsy is performed to evaluate for lupus nephritis.
Diagnosis: Kidney, native, biopsy: Lupus Nephritis, Class IV-G (A)
Light Microscopy Description: The specimen consists of two cores of renal cortex and medulla. Up to 28 glomeruli are identified for evaluation. All glomeruli show global, diffuse endocapillary and mesangial hypercellularity with neutrophilic infiltration. Multiple glomeruli contain wire loop lesions. There is moderate tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis involving approximately 30% of the cortex. No crescents or fibrinoid necrosis are seen.
Immunofluorescence Description:
IgG: 3+granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops (full house pattern). IgA: 2+granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops. IgM: 2+granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops. C3: 3+granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops. C1q: 2+granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops. Fibrinogen: Negative. Albumin: Negative.
Electron Microscopy Description: Electron microscopy confi cies diffuse subendothelial and mesangial election-dense deposits. Tubuloreticular inclusions are present within endothelial cells. There is approximately 50% podocyte foot process effacement.
Comment: The combined findings are diagnostic of active, diffuse global lupus nephritis. ISN/RPS 2003 Class IV-G (A).
Specimen: Native kidney biopsy

Clinical History: 45-year-old female with a 2.5 cm solid, hypoechoic nodule in the right lobe of the thyroid, discovered on ultrasound.
Diagnosis: Thyroid, Right Lobe, Fine-Needle Aspiration: Suspicious for Malignancy (Bethesda Category V).
Specimen Adequacy: The specimen is adequate for evaluation.
Microscopic Description: The aspirate is cellular and shows crowded clusters of follicular cells with a microfollicular architecture. The cells exhibit nuclear enlargement, chromatin pallor, and irregular nuclear contours. Occasional nuclear grooves and rare intranuclear cytoplasmic pseudoinclusions are identified. Comment: The cytomorphologic features are suspicious for papillary thyroid carcinoma. Per the Bethesda System for Reporting Thyroid Cytopathology, surgical excision is recommended for definitive diagnosis.

Polysomnography Report
Procedure: Attended, full-night diagnostic polysomnography.
Clinical Indication: Excessive daytime sleepiness, reported snoring, and witnessed apneas.
This was a technically adequate overnight diagnostic polysomnogram. Total sleep time was 345 minutes with a sleep efficiency of 82%. Sleep architecture was abnormal due to significant sleep fragmentation. REM sleep was reduced, comprising only 10% of total sleep time.
Frequent respiratory events were noted throughout the night. The overall Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) was 42 events per hour, which is in the severe range. These events were predominantly obstructive apneas and hypopneas, and they were more severe during REM sleep. This was associated with significant oxygen desaturation, with a nadir SpO2 of 78%. The patient's baseline oxygen saturation was 95%. No significant periodic limb movements were noted.
The findings are consistent with severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).
A follow-up appointment is recommended to discuss treatment options, including positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy. A subsequent PAP titration study under polysomnography is indicated to determine the optimal pressure for treatment.

Histologic sections reveal cores of breast tissue with an infiltrative neoplasm. The tumor cells are arranged in irregular nests and single files, infiltrating the fibrous stroma. Invasive Ductal Carcinoma, Grade 3 of 3.

Diet: You may resume your normal diet as tolerated. Start with clear liquids and light foods (e.g., soup, gelatin, crackers) and advance to a regular diet if you are not experiencing nausea or significant bloating. Avoid heavy, greasy, or spicy foods for the first 24 hours.
Follow-up: Based on the normal findings of your colonoscopy, your next routine screening colonoscopy is recommended in 10 years. We will send a reminder to you at that time. If you experience any severe abdominal pain, persistent nausea or vomiting, fever, or significant rectal bleeding, please contact our office immediately or go to the nearest emergency room.

Impression: Full-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL). Complex, displaced tear of the medial meniscus with a large fragment. Moderate joint effusion. Bone contusions consistent with a pivot-shift injury.

Immediate Post-Procedure Care
Transportation: You must be discharged into the care of a responsible adult who will drive you home. You are not permitted to drive, take a taxi or rideshare alone, or use public transportation by yourself.

Begin by drinking clear liquids (such as water, apple juice, ginger ale, or broth) once you are home.

Diet: You may resume your normal diet as tolerated. Start with clear liquids and light foods (e.g., soup, gelatin, crackers) and advance to a regular diet if you are not experiencing nausea or significant bloating. Avoid heavy, greasy, or spicy foods for the first 24 hours.
Follow-up: Based on the normal findings of your colonoscopy, your next routine screening colonoscopy is recommended in 10 years. We will send a reminder to you at that time. Clinical History: 29-year-old female with a known history of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), presenting with new-onset proteinuria and hematuria. Biopsy is performed to evaluate for lupus nephritis.
Diagnosis: Kidney, native, biopsy: Lupus Nephritis, Class IV-G (A)
Light Microscopy Description: The specimen consists of two cores of renal cortex and medulla. Up to 28 glomeruli are identified for evaluation. All glomeruli show global, diffuse endocapillary and mesangial hypercellularity with neutrophilic infiltration. Multiple glomeruli contain wire loop lesions. There is moderate tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis involving approximately 30% of the cortex. No crescent or fibrinoid necrosis are seen.
Immunofluorescence Description:
IgG: 3+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops (full house pattern).
IgA: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops. IgM: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops. C3: 3+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops. C1q: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.
Fibrinogen: Negative.
Albumin: Negative.
Electron Microscopy Description: Electron microscopy confirms diffuse subendothelial and mesangial electron-dense deposits. Tubuloreticular inclusions are present within endothelial cells. There is approximately 50% podocyte foot process effacement.
Comment: The combined findings are diagnostic of active, diffuse global lupus nephritis, ISN/RPS
2003 Class IV-G (A).
Specimen: Native kidney biopsy

Clinical History: 28-year-old female with a one-month history of a painless, enlarging left-sided neck mass. Associated with night sweats. Concern for lymphoma. Diagnosis: Lymph Node, Left Cervical, Excision: Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma, Nodular Sclerosis Type.
Gross Description: Received fresh, labeled 'left neck mass,' is an encapsulated lymph node measuring 2.8 x 2.1 x 1.5 cm. The cut surface is tan-white and firm, with a vaguely nodular appearance. Microscopic Description: Sections of the lymph node show complete effacement of the normal architecture by a nodular infiltrate. The nodules are defined by broad bands of collagenous fibrosis. Within the nodules, there is a mixed inflammatory background composed of small lymphocytes, eosinophils, and histiocytes. Scattered throughout this background are large, atypical cells, including classic binucleated Reed-Sternberg cells and their mononuclear variants (Hodgkin cells). These cells have large, vesicular nuclei, prominent eosinophilic nucleoli, and abundant cytoplasm. Immunohistochemistry: The large, atypical cells show the following immunophenotype:
CD15: Positive
PAX5: Positive (dim)
CD45: Negative
CD20: Negative
CD3: Highlights the background T-cell population.
Comment: The morphologic findings in conjunction with the immunophenotype (CD30+, CD15+, PAX5+, CD45-) are diagnostic of Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma, Nodular Sclerosis subtype. Clinical correlation and appropriate oncologic management are recommended.
Specimen: Left cervical lymph
node
